title: Buyer-side measurements from 25,011 paid x402 calls on Base mainnet, including duplicate settlement on one intent
quote: 25,011 paid calls to 1,036 sellers, about 135 USDC; 1,587 failed the buyer: 6.3% [6.0%, 6.7%] by count (live)... We sent one purchase intent twice, back to back, with fresh signatures, to 10 sellers. 5 of 10 settled both. In a second test we dropped the connection after 2 seconds and retried as a plain client would; the retry produced a second settlement at 5 of 10.

title: [Bug]: @x402/fetch client signs and submits a payment for ANY amount the server declares in the 402 requirements
quote: a server that inflates the payment requirement to x10 the resource's canonical price gets paid exactly that inflated amount by the official client... the only protection that engaged was the caller-configured spend limit

title: Check what your AI agents do before they do it, with Semantic governance policies
quote: Semantic governance policies, available in Preview in Gemini platform... check each tool call an agent proposes against what the user asked for and against rules you write in plain language... If it doesn't [pass], the engine replaces the response's content, tool calls included, with a configurable denial message... Either way, the verdict and the judge's rationale go to Cloud Logging in your project.

title: Agent Anomaly Detection: Safeguarding agents across other clouds
quote: Agent Anomaly Detection is in Private Preview, including monitoring for agents that run outside Google Cloud... An agent outside Google Cloud needs... a Google identity without a service account key [via] Workload Identity Federation... In another, a user pasted an order note that said 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE,' and the agent refunded $999 on a $15.99 order.

title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
quote: Bloomberg reports that macOS 27.3 will warn users against granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple told developers it would 'introduce additional controls' and require 'very explicit user action' for that access... the in-house agent 'remains in the early stages.'
